Proof in the paper: The XRD patterns of NixZnyAl (Fig. 2) show peaks due to metallic Ni at 2θ = 44.5, 51.8, and 76.4° (PDF#04-0850) for Ni3Zn0Al. In contrast, they shifted to low angles as the Ni/Zn atomic ratio decreased from 50/1 to 2/1, indicating the incorporation of Zn atoms into the metallic Ni lattice to form the Ni-rich alloy, a substitutional solid solution with a face-centered cubic (fcc) structure (space group of Fm-3m). An IMC with tetragonal L10 structure (denoted as t-NiZn, space group of I4/mmm (139)), corresponding to the peaks at 2θ = 43.5, 46.7, and 84.4°C (PDF#06-0672), formed in Ni1Zn1Al and Ni1Zn2Al, and a cubic NiZn IMC (denoted as c-NiZn, space group of Pm–3m (221)) with peaks at 2θ = 43.5, 63.8, and 80.5°C (PDF#65-3203) formed in Ni1Zn8Al. HAADF-STEM images and corresponding EDS mapping (Fig. 3) reveal that Ni and Zn atoms are uniformly distributed in Ni1Zn1Al.
